title: Workflows vs agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow involves no language model, while an agent is built around a language model
A workflow makes a single model call, while an agent keeps calling the model repeatedly
A workflow follows steps its code sets in advance, while an agent's model picks its own next step
A workflow cannot call tools, while an agent can call tools to take actions

items.stem: Your assistant's Python code sends each student message to the model and asks it to reply with one label: booking, manual_question or other. The code then runs a pipeline you wrote for that label; for booking it always runs check_calendar, then check_training_record, then create_booking. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: A workflow: the model only picks a label, and the code defines every path and what runs next
An agent: the model's label decides which branch runs, so the model controls the flow
An agent: the model is called more than once for a single request, so it is a loop
A workflow: the model is not used to take any actions, and agents are the ones that act

items.stem: Booking requests currently go through a fixed workflow of 3 model calls. A teammate's agent version handles the same requests with 7 model calls on average. Assume every model call costs $0.004 and ignore the cost of running tools. For 500 booking requests, how much more does the agent version cost than the workflow, in dollars?
Which part of the makerspace assistant is the strongest candidate for a fixed workflow, if the goal is low and predictable cost per request?

options.text: Answering a student's question that might need the manuals, the calendar, or both
Diagnosing a machine fault that a student describes only vaguely
Planning a project that spans several machines over several weeks
Confirming a booking: check the slot, check the training, create the entry, send the receipt

items.stem: Which is the best reason to choose an agent over a fixed workflow for part of a system?

options.text: The budget is small, since an agent takes only the steps it needs
The steps needed differ by request and cannot be listed in advance
The task has many steps, and a workflow can only handle a few
The output must be as repeatable as possible from one request to the next

items.stem: The assistant has two jobs: a booking sequence that is the same every time, and open-ended help with questions about machines. What architecture would you defend at the design review?

options.text: One agent for both jobs, since an agent can also follow a fixed sequence
One fixed workflow for both jobs, since workflows have the most predictable cost
A fixed workflow for the booking sequence and an agent for the open-ended questions
A separate agent for each job, so a model chooses the steps in both
